item.title: Thursday, September 3, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk. One, the FOMC meets 15-16 September, twelve days out, so lock or float decisions on anything closing inside three weeks should be made this week; note the 30-year fixed sits about 210bp over the 10-year against a long-run norm nearer 170bp, so a Treasury rally will not pass through one-for-one. Two, underwrite Q4 on today's rates: August private payrolls came in at 38,000, the softest since January, and the 10-year still did not rally, meaning oil and supply are pricing the long end rather than the Fed. Three, if you have multifamily to bring to market, bring it now: 36.7 billion dollars traded in the first half, agency debt is still writing cheques as the 20.6 million dollar Freddie Mac loan on the Seattle trade shows, and rising sale-leaseback volume means competing product is coming. And three things for the world. One, the United States struck Iran on 1 September, Iran retaliated across Bahrain, Jordan and Iraq, and four American service members were confirmed killed; that conflict is now the biggest single input into the oil price. Two, the House rejected a constitutional amendment to cap the Supreme Court at nine justices, 212 votes to 206. Three, Real Madrid spent roughly 200 million pounds this summer, released Dani Carvajal after 451 appearances, and have opened the season with three wins from three.

item.title: Tuesday, August 25, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk. One: Kevin Warsh delivers his first Jackson Hole keynote as Fed Chair on Friday 28 August at 10am ET — have the lock conversation with floating clients today or tomorrow, not Thursday afternoon. Two: quote the daily tracker at 6.77%, not the Freddie Mac weekly survey at 6.65% — the survey lags and clients arrive with the wrong expectation. Three: the mortgage spread is 207 basis points against a historical norm nearer 170, so the next third of a point of relief comes from spread compression rather than a Fed cut; and on commercial, price to today's debt cost — a Washington DC office tower at 1250 Connecticut Ave NW just went to foreclosure sale. Also in this episode: Treasury Secretary Bessent's "Operation Economic Outcast" sanctions campaign against Iran and Tehran's threatened Strait of Hormuz toll, with Brent at $94.12; the Supreme Court lifting one of two injunctions on the mail-in voting executive order ahead of the midterms; a mixed Monday tape with the Nasdaq down 0.8% on a chip sell-off ahead of Nvidia's Wednesday print; NJ Transit's 3% July fare rise and Mayor Mamdani's Brooklyn-Queens Expressway move; the weekend box office led by Spider-Man: Brand New Day at $39m; and Real Madrid opening La Liga with a 2-1 win at Espanyol, Carlos Espi scoring a stoppage-time winner on debut under new manager Jose Mourinho.

item.title: Monday, August 24, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk. One: Freddie Mac's next survey lands Thursday, so you have three days — rates are at 6.65 percent and easing gently, but Kevin Warsh has just debuted at Jackson Hole into a market debating hike risk rather than cuts, so any client waiting for materially cheaper money this autumn is waiting on something the market is not pricing; have that conversation before Thursday. Two: the Northeast median is up 5.2 percent year over year against a national 2.0 percent — more than double, the strongest regional gain in the country — so put it in your next listing presentation and seller conversation this week. Three: inventory sits at 4.6 months and days on market have ticked up to 29, with a quarter of the market paying cash, so reset seller expectations now rather than in October. And three things for the world. One: Kevin Warsh has given his first Jackson Hole address as Fed Chairman, and the live argument is about a possible hike, not a cut. Two: Iran has threatened to halt oil exports entirely and its parliament is advancing tolls on the Strait of Hormuz as Washington readies what Scott Bessent calls an economic D-Day, with Brent near 94 dollars. Three: Bitcoin just had a 22 percent week, and Spider-Man has held the box office top spot for a fourth straight weekend.

item.title: Friday, August 14, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk. The thirty-year fixed fell to 6.67 percent, its first drop in six weeks, and borrowers are moving on tiny changes, so call the fence-sitters today. New Jersey price reductions are up nearly 20 percent year over year with inventory up 14 percent, so have the pricing conversation with sellers in week one, especially in Bergen and Morris, while Sussex runs the opposite way. And New York's pied-a-terre fight is live with the tax possibly rolling out during appeal, so clients eyeing a Manhattan second home above five million dollars need advice now. Also inside: the September Fed debate is about a hike rather than a cut, the Strait of Hormuz is still barely open, the S&P 500 cleared 7,800 for the first time, Spider-Man: Brand New Day passed a billion, and Real Madrid signed Yan Diomande for a club record.

item.title: Saturday, August 8, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk. One: Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac's revised condo project standards are landing this month, eliminating the limited review path and lifting reserves to 15% of budget — confirm the effective date with your lender Monday and assume a full review on every August and September condo closing. Two: the daily 30-year tracker sits at 6.91% while Freddie Mac's Thursday survey printed 6.69%, a 22bp gap the wrong way round, so get ahead of the client who quotes you the lower number. Three: the September Fed question is a hike, not a cut — Friday's weak jobs report bought borrowers time, not a rally, so expiring locks should close today. And three things for the world. One: US employers cut 23,000 jobs in July with a further 103,000 revised off prior months, unemployment at 4.1%, and the S&P 500 hit a record 7,757 precisely because weak data cools rate-hike odds. Two: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed a mutual defence pact in Mecca with an attack-on-one-is-an-attack-on-all clause, in the middle of the Iran war, with Hormuz traffic down to 33 vessels from 50. Three: the Senate passed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act and sent it to the House, targeting buyers of Russian oil. Also inside: Vinicius Junior extends at Real Madrid to June 2032, Spider-Man Brand New Day's $355m opening and a record $429m weekend, and the Port Authority's $45bn capital plan.

item.title: Friday, August 7, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk. One: the survey and the screen disagree — Freddie Mac has the thirty-year fixed at 6.69 percent and a one-year high, while the Mortgage News Daily index has it at 6.75 percent and drifting lower for a fortnight, so any buyer who read the AP headline needs that explained before they cancel a weekend viewing. Two: the mortgage spread is doing the damage, not the Treasury — roughly 2.1 percentage points over a 4.63 percent ten-year, which is wide, so price your conversations for rates staying in this neighbourhood through the autumn rather than promising a break. Three: institutional and household money have decoupled — Manhattan investment sales ran 10 billion dollars in the first half, up 50 percent, while residential mortgage demand has fallen below year-ago levels. Also in this episode: the Trump-Hegseth Camp David row over Iran munitions, the Iran-Oman Strait of Hormuz corridor and the oil whipsaw, Abdul El-Sayed's upset win in Michigan's Democratic Senate primary, Erica Schwartz confirmed as CDC director 51-44 amid a 35-year measles high, Austria's back-to-back national heat records, a record-setting week on Wall Street that lost its nerve on Thursday, Mamdani and the Mayor's Fund, the biggest box office weekend in history, and Real Madrid's club-record signing of Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig.

item.title: Thursday, August 6, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk. One: the Freddie Mac survey hit a one-year high of 6.66% for the 30-year fixed, up 8 basis points, and a fresh survey prints today — so quote the live daily tracker at 6.75% to clients this week, not the stale survey number. Two: mortgage applications fell 2.9% last week and total demand is now running below year-ago levels, so go back to pre-approved buyers now and tell them the June quote is not the September rate. Three: CMBS delinquencies spiked in July and distress is rising — any client with commercial debt maturing inside twelve months should open the refinance conversation now, because early is a negotiation and late is a workout. And three things for the world: Iran and Strait of Hormuz diplomacy is currently the strongest force in global markets, pushing oil and Treasury yields down and Wall Street to record highs; the Gaza ceasefire is faltering after Hamas agreed to disarm and strikes followed the next day; and Disney's streaming profit more than doubled to 712 million dollars while both Disney and Netflix have stopped publishing the subscriber and viewership figures they once boasted about. Plus a record box office weekend, Mourinho's 2-2 Real Madrid debut, Salah joining Trabzonspor on a free, and a New York City heat emergency in effect today.

item.title: Wednesday, August 5, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk. One: the Freddie Mac survey prints Thursday and the odds of a September Fed hike are running above sixty percent, so any client sitting on a float should have the lock conversation today. Two: the New York City pied-a-terre tax exemption deadline has moved to 18 September, so call every client with a second home valued above five million dollars, because only seventeen thousand of nine hundred thousand flagged properties received a letter and not receiving one is not proof of safety. Three: New Jersey inventory is up nearly five percent, days on market are five days longer at forty-one, and the share of list price received has slipped to 101.3 percent, so reset seller expectations at the listing appointment this week. And three things for the world. One: the Federal Reserve's dissenters are now voting for hikes rather than cuts, reversing the direction of the whole argument. Two: Iran and Oman are close to a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which knocked six percent off crude and helped push the S&P 500, Dow and Nasdaq to record closes. Three: Spider-Man: Brand New Day opened to 360.1 million dollars domestically in a single weekend.

item.title: Tuesday, August 4, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk. One: mortgage rates are flat at roughly 6.65 percent only because the mortgage-to-Treasury spread is absorbing a rising 10-year, now at 4.71 percent and up about 49 basis points year over year — that cushion is thinning, so lock risk is asymmetric this week. Two: Northeast inventory is rising while prices hold, meaning listings now compete with each other — reset seller pricing and days-on-market expectations before the autumn season, not during it. Three: New York office-to-residential conversions are on track to more than double this year on the back of the 467-m tax incentive, City of Yes zoning and repriced office assets — that is where commercial deal flow is. Also in this episode: the Fed's divided July 29 hold under Chair Kevin Warsh, US-Iran escalation and talks, the rare US-Japan joint yen intervention, a record 434 million dollar box office weekend led by Spider-Man Brand New Day, and Jose Mourinho's first match back at Real Madrid.

item.title: Monday, August 3, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk. One, Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac have tightened condominium project review, so if you have a condo under contract in a building with thin reserves or a recent special assessment, call your lender today and confirm the file still clears. Two, stop promising an autumn refinance: the Fed held on July 29 with an openly divided committee, and the odds that moved afterwards were September hike odds, not cut odds, with the 30-year fixed flat at 6.65 percent and Freddie Mac's survey at 6.66 percent. Three, watch the New Jersey employment tape, with roughly 2,400 layoffs announced in July and Mars Wrigley moving 307 jobs to Chicago. And three things for the world. American strikes on Iran were called off with direct talks resuming Monday and Oman mediating separately on the Strait of Hormuz. A fifteen-point Hamas disarmament roadmap was announced July 31, and Israeli strikes killed seven in Gaza on August 1. And Spider-Man Brand New Day opened to 355 million dollars domestically, the second biggest opening weekend in box office history, in a record 429 million dollar weekend for North American cinemas.

item.title: Sunday, August 2, 2026

item.title: Thursday, July 30, 2026
item.description: Three things for the desk. One: Freddie Mac's weekly print lands at noon Eastern today and, after the Fed's divided hold and the bond sell-off that followed it, assume it goes up — call anyone with a rate lock expiring in the next fortnight before they read it elsewhere. Two: pending home sales fell five point four percent in June while Northeast inventory rose, so price new listings to actual comparable sales rather than to spring's optimism. Three: split your New York advice by product rather than by borough — luxury is surging on cash while co-ops stall on financing and board approval. And three things for the world. One: the Fed held at three point five zero to three point seven five percent, but three officials dissented in favour of a hike, so the debate is no longer about how fast rates come down. Two: southern Europe has evacuated more than three hundred and sixty thousand people and burned nearly three hundred thousand acres in a second heat wave at one hundred and seven Fahrenheit. Three: Spain are world champions, having beaten Argentina one nil at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.
